description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:660 calls `<Certificate as der::Decode>::from_der(&der)` using fully-qualified syntax because the `Decode` trait is not in scope at the file level. The two functions in this file that decode DER values both use a different style:

- aia_extract.rs:20 imports `use der::{asn1::ObjectIdentifier, Decode};` and then writes `AuthorityInfoAccessSyntax::from_der(extn_value)` (line 48) — idiomatic method-call form.
- lib.rs:1485 and 1563 use `use x509_cert::der::Decode as _;` inside the function scope, then `ExtendedKeyUsage::from_der(...)` and `KeyUsage::from_der(...)`.
- lib.rs:660 uses the UFCS form `<Certificate as der::Decode>::from_der(&der)` with no `use` statement at all.

UFCS is correct, but it is the noisy escape hatch you reach for when there is a name conflict — there is none here. The straightforward `use der::Decode as _;` at the top of the file (or inside `build_with_aia`) eliminates the angle-bracket dance and matches the style used elsewhere in the same module.

What goes wrong if it stays: readability cost on every `Certificate` parse site; the inconsistency between the three styles signals that the file evolved over time without a unifying style choice. A future maintainer adding another `from_der` call has three precedents to pick from.
title: UFCS <Certificate as der::Decode>::from_der instead of trait-import + method-call
